newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends down on CBOT as crusher, Japan buy.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends down on CBOT as crusher, Japan buy.

text.p: WCE canola futures ended lower, pulled down by a drop in CBOT soybean futures, traders said.
However, declines were curbed by crusher buying and by Japanese demand for canola on the cash market.

"We followed Chicago and a commission house sold 1,000 contracts, crushers bought 2,500 to 3,000 across the board and there was strong export demand," a trader said. May WCE futures crush profit margin fell to -14.06 Wednesday from -4.74 Tuesday. Mar-May spread at $5, May-July $0.70, May-July $55. Volume was 13,165, or 263,300 tonnes, with 2,800 hedges.
Japan bought 20,000 tonnes canola overnight, some sources said, while others pegged the Japanese purchase at 30,000 tonnes. One source put the Japanese purchase at 50,000 tonnes.
May canola lost $4.10 to $424.20, July fell $3.10 to $425.50. May flax lost $4.20 to $357 on hedges in light trade.
March feed wheat was unchanged at $177.50 on commercial demand, May lost $2.80 to $169.20. Mar-May spread at $7.50, Mar-July $9. Volume was 845 lots. Oats did not trade.
March western barley fell $2.10 to $141.90 on U.S. corn, May lost $2.10 to $142.90 with UGG and Alberta Wheat Pool buying, traders said. Mar-May spread at $1. Volume was 1,100.
UGG sold May feed peas down US$0.50 to US$211. Volume 75.
(All values in Canadian dollars, except feed peas)
